body.text: Tattvasamāsasūtravṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Tattvasamāsasūtravṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Aphorisms of the Compendium of Principles).

children.translated_text: He who, among the twenty-five principles (<s>tattvas</s>), obtained knowledge from birth,
to that great sage <s>Kapila</s>, [who appeared] at the first creation, salutations! // 1 //

body.text:
athātastattvasamāsākhyasāṅkhyasūtrāṇi vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
iha kaścidbrāhmaṇastrividhena duḥkhenābhibhūtaḥ sāṅkhyācāryaṃ kapilamaharṣiṃ śaraṇamupāgataḥ | svakulanāmagotrasvādhyāyaṃ nivedyāha |
bhagavan kimiha paraṃ kiṃ yāthātathyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyaḥ syāmiti |
kapila uvāca kathayiṣyāmi |
body.translated_text: Now, therefore, we shall expound the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> aphorisms (<s>sūtras</s>) known as the <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> (Compendium of Principles). Here, a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, overcome by the threefold suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), approached the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> teacher, the great sage <s>Kapila</s>, as his refuge. Having announced his family, name, lineage (<s>gotra</s>), and Vedic recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), he said: 'O lord (<s>Bhagavan</s>), what is the highest [truth] here? What is the true nature of reality (<s>yāthātathya</s>)? Having done what, would I become one who has accomplished his purpose?' <s>Kapila</s> said: 'I shall explain.'

body.text: aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ || Tats_1 ||
body.translated_text: The eight root-principles (<s>prakṛtis</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_1 ||

body.text: ṣoḍaśa vikārāḥ || Tats_2 ||

body.translated_text: The creation of beings (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) of fourteen kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_18 ||

body.translated_text: The elemental creation (<s>dhātusarga</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_19 ||

body.translated_text: Bondage (<s>bandha</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_20 ||

body.translated_text: Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_23 ||

children.text: etat paramparayā yāthātathyametat samyag jñātvā kṛtakṛtyaḥ syānna punastrividhena duḥkhenābhibhūyate |
children.translated_text: Having truly known this [teaching] through tradition (<s>paramparā</s>), which is the true nature of reality (<s>yāthātathya</s>), one becomes one who has accomplished his purpose and is no longer overcome by the threefold suffering.
Thus [end] the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> aphorisms known as the <s>Tattvasamāsa</s>. ||
[The eight root-principles (<s>prakṛtis</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_1 ||]

body.text:
atha kā aṣṭau prakṛtaya ityatrocyate |
avyaktaṃ buddhirahaṅkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇītyetā aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ |
tatrāvyaktaṃ tāvaducyate yathā loke vyajyante ghaṭapaṭakuḍyaśayanakādyā na tathā vyajata ityavyaktam | śrotrādibhirindriyairna gṛhyata ityarthaḥ |
kasmāt anādimadhyāntatvānniravayavatvācca ||
body.translated_text: Now, what are the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (root-principles)? To this it is said: The Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>), Intellect (<s>Buddhi</s>), Ego-sense (<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>), and the five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) — these are the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>. Among these, the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>) is first explained: just as in the world, pots, cloths, walls, beds, and such things are manifest, it is not manifest in that way — hence 'unmanifest.' It is not grasped by the sense organs such as hearing etc. — that is the meaning. Why? Because it is without beginning, middle, or end, and because it is without parts (<s>niravayava</s>). ||

children.translated_text: Without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, likewise eternal, devoid of taste and smell,

children.text: anādimadhyaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ pradhānametat pravadanti sūrayaḥ //
children.translated_text: without beginning or middle, higher than the Great (<s>Mahat</s>), permanent — the wise call this <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal substance). //

body.text:
sūkṣmamaliṅgamacetanamanādinidhanaṃ tathāprasavadharmi niravayavamekameva hi sādhāraṇametadavyaktam |
avyaktasyāmī paryāyaśabdā bhavanti |
avyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ brahma paraṃ dhruvaṃ bahudhānakamakṣaraṃ kṣetraṃ tamaḥprasūtamiti |
body.translated_text: It is subtle, without distinguishing marks (<s>aliṅga</s>), unconscious (<s>acetana</s>), without beginning or end, likewise having the nature of production (<s>prasavadharmi</s>), without parts, one and undivided, and common [to all effects] — this is the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>). These are the synonymous terms for the Unmanifest: <s>Avyakta</s> (the Unmanifest), <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Substance), <s>Brahma</s>, the Supreme, the Permanent (<s>Dhruva</s>), the Manifold (<s>Bahudhānaka</s>), the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), the Field (<s>Kṣetra</s>), and Born of Darkness (<s>Tamaḥprasūta</s>).

body.text:
kā buddhiratrocyate |
adhyavasāyo buddhiḥ |
soyamadhyavasāyo gavādiṣu dravyeṣu yasmāt pratipattiḥ |
evametannānyathā |
gaurevāyaṃ nāśvaḥ |
sthāṇurevāyaṃ na puruṣaḥ |
ityeṣā buddhiḥ |
asyāstu buddheraṣṭau rūpāṇi bhavanti dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryamiti |
tatra dharmo nāmādharmaviparyayaḥ śrutismṛtivihitaḥ śiṣṭācārāviruddhaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ |
jñānaṃ nāmājñānaviparyayastattvabhāvabhūtānāṃ sambodhaḥ |
vairāgyaṃ nāmāvairāgyaviparyayaḥ śabdādiviṣayeṣvaprasaktiḥ |
aiśvaryaṃ nāmānaiśvaryaviparyayo 'ṇimādayo 'ṣṭaguṇāḥ |
etāni sāttvikāni catvāri |
adharmo 'jñānamavairāgyamanaiśvaryamiti adharmo nāma dharmaviparyayaḥ śrutismṛtiviruddhaḥ śiṣṭācāraviruddho 'śubhalakṣaṇaḥ |
ajñānaṃ nāma jñānaviparyayastattvabhāvabhūtānāmanavabodhaḥ |
avairāgyaṃ nāma vairāgyaviparyaḥ śabdādiviṣayeṣvabhiṣaṅgaḥ |
anaiśvaryaṃ nāmaiśvaryaviparyayo 'ṇimādirahitatvam |
etāni tāmasāni catvāri |
tatra dharmeṇa nimittenordhvagamanam |
jñānena nimittena mokṣaḥ |
vairāgyeṇa nimittena prakṛtilayaḥ |
aiśvaryanimittenā 'pratihatagatirbhavati |

children.translated_text: Thus this eight-formed <s>Buddhi</s> (Intellect) has been explained.
These are the synonymous terms for <s>Buddhi</s>:

children.text: mano matirmahān brahmā khyātiḥ prajñā śrutirdhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Manas</s> (mind), <s>Mati</s> (thought), <s>Mahān</s> (the Great), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>Śruti</s> (learning), <s>Dhṛti</s> (steadiness),
<s>Prajñāna</s> (awareness), <s>Santati</s> (continuity), <s>Smṛti</s> (memory), <s>Dhī</s> (intelligence) — [these] are declared [as synonyms of] <s>Buddhi</s>. //

body.translated_text: What is <s>Buddhi</s> (Intellect)? To this it is said: Determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is <s>Buddhi</s>. This determination is that by which there is cognition with regard to substances such as cows etc.: 'It is thus and not otherwise; this is indeed a cow, not a horse; this is indeed a post, not a person' — this is <s>Buddhi</s>. And this <s>Buddhi</s> has eight forms: <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). Among these, <s>dharma</s> is the opposite of <s>adharma</s> (vice), prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), not contrary to the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>), characterized by auspiciousness. <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) is the opposite of <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), the awakening to the true nature of the principles (<s>tattvas</s>). <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion) is the opposite of <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), non-attachment to objects such as sound etc. <s>Aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) is the opposite of <s>anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness), the eight powers (<s>guṇas</s>) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness). These four are <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>). <s>Adharma</s>, <s>ajñāna</s>, <s>avairāgya</s>, and <s>anaiśvarya</s> — <s>adharma</s> is the opposite of <s>dharma</s>, contrary to <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, contrary to the conduct of the learned, characterized by inauspiciousness. <s>Ajñāna</s> (ignorance) is the opposite of <s>jñāna</s>, the non-awakening to the true nature of the principles. <s>Avairāgya</s> (attachment) is the opposite of <s>vairāgya</s>, clinging to objects such as sound etc. <s>Anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness) is the opposite of <s>aiśvarya</s>, being devoid of [the powers] beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>. These four are <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>). Among these: by <s>dharma</s> as the cause, there is upward movement [to higher realms]; by <s>jñāna</s> as the cause, there is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>); by <s>vairāgya</s> as the cause, there is dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>); by <s>aiśvarya</s> as the cause, one attains unobstructed movement.

body.text:
atrāha ko 'haṅkāra ityucyate |
abhimāno 'haṅkāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense)? To this it is said: Self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>) is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ śabde ahaṃ sparśe ahaṃ rūpe ahaṃ rase /
children.translated_text: 'I [am in] sound, I [am in] touch, I [am in] form, I [am in] taste,
I [am in] smell, I am the master, I am wealthy, I am the lord.' // 1 //

children.text: ahaṃ bhogī ahaṃ dharme 'bhiṣikto 'sau mayā hataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am the enjoyer, I [am established] in <s>dharma</s>, I am the anointed [king], he was slain by me,
I shall slay [him]; [I shall prevail] over powerful enemies' — such and similar [notions constitute <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>]. // 2 //
This cognition of self-conceit (<s>abhimāna-pratyaya</s>) is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense).
These are the synonymous terms for <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>:

<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>Vaikārika</s> (the modified), <s>Taijasa</s> (the luminous), <s>Bhūtādi</s> (the origin of elements), with inference (<s>sānumāna</s>), and without inference (<s>niranumāna</s>). ||

body.text:
atrāha kāni pañcatanmātrāṇītyucyate |
ahaṅkārānvitāni pañcatanmātrāṇi śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātraṃ ceti pañcatanmātrāṇi |
tatra tāvacchabdatanmātrāṇi śabdeṣvevopalabhyante udāttānudāttasvaritakampitaṣaḍjarṣabhagāndhāramadhyamapañcamadhaivataniṣādādayaḥ śabdaviśeṣādupalabhyante |
tasmācchabdatanmātre 'viśeṣaḥ |
atha sparśatanmātrāṇi sparśeṣvevopalabhyante tatra mṛdukaṭhinakarkaśapicchilaśītoṣṇādayaḥ sparśaviśeṣā upalabhyante |
tasmāt sparśatanmātre 'viśeṣaḥ |
rūpatanmātrāṇi rūpeṣvevopalabhyante |
tatra śuklaraktakṛṣṇaharitapītahāridramāñjiṣṭhādayo rūpaviśeṣā upalabhyante |
tasmādrūpatanmātre 'viśeṣaḥ |
tathā rasatanmātrāṇi raseṣvevopalabhyante |
tatra kaṭutiktakaṣāyakṣāramadhurāmlalavaṇādayo rasaviśeṣā upalabhyante |
tasmādrasatanmātre 'viśeṣaḥ |
atha gandhatanmātrāṇi gandha evopalabhyante |
tatra surabhirasurabhiśca gandhaviśeṣā upalabhyante |
tasmād gandhatanmātre 'viśeṣaḥ |
evametatpañcatanmātrāṇi sūcitāni |
athaiṣāṃ paryāyaśabdāḥ |
tanmātrāṇyaviśeṣāṇi mahābhūtaprakṛtayo bhogyānyaṇavaḥ śāntaghoramūḍhānīti |
evametā avyaktabuddhyahaṃkāratanmātrasañjñitā aṣṭau prakṛtayo vyākhyātāḥ |
atha kasmāt prakṛtayaḥ |
prakurvantīti prakṛtayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what are the five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>)? To this it is said: Connected with <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, the five <s>tanmātras</s> are: the subtle element of sound (<s>śabda-tanmātra</s>), the subtle element of touch (<s>sparśa-tanmātra</s>), the subtle element of form (<s>rūpa-tanmātra</s>), the subtle element of taste (<s>rasa-tanmātra</s>), and the subtle element of smell (<s>gandha-tanmātra</s>) — these are the five <s>tanmātras</s>. Among these, first, the subtle elements of sound are perceived only in sounds — the specific varieties of sound perceived are: <s>udātta</s> (raised), <s>anudātta</s> (unraised), <s>svarita</s> (circumflex), <s>kampita</s> (tremulous), <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, <s>niṣāda</s>, etc. Therefore, in the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> there is no specific differentiation. Now, the subtle elements of touch are perceived only in touches — the specific varieties of touch perceived are: soft, hard, rough, slimy, cold, hot, etc. Therefore, in the <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> there is no specific differentiation. The subtle elements of form are perceived only in forms — the specific varieties of form perceived are: white, red, black, green, yellow, turmeric-colored, madder-colored, etc. Therefore, in the <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> there is no specific differentiation. Likewise, the subtle elements of taste are perceived only in tastes — the specific varieties of taste perceived are: pungent, bitter, astringent, alkaline, sweet, sour, salty, etc. Therefore, in the <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> there is no specific differentiation. Now, the subtle elements of smell are perceived only in smells — the specific varieties of smell perceived are: fragrant and non-fragrant. Therefore, in the <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> there is no specific differentiation. Thus these five <s>tanmātras</s> have been indicated. Now, their synonymous terms: <s>tanmātras</s>, non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), origins of the great elements (<s>mahābhūta-prakṛti</s>), objects of experience (<s>bhogya</s>), atoms (<s>aṇu</s>), peaceful-fierce-dull (<s>śānta-ghora-mūḍha</s>). Thus these eight <s>prakṛtis</s> designated as Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>), Intellect (<s>Buddhi</s>), Ego-sense (<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>), and Subtle Elements (<s>Tanmātra</s>) have been explained. Now, why are they called <s>prakṛtis</s>? Because they produce (<s>prakurvanti</s>) — [therefore they are] <s>prakṛtis</s>.

children.translated_text: [The sixteen modifications (<s>vikāras</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_2 ||]

body.text:

ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcamahābhūtānyete ṣoḍaśavikārāḥ |

vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthākhyāni pañca karmendriyāṇi svaṃ svaṃ karma kurvanti |
tatra vāgvacanamuccarati |
hastau karma kurutaḥ |
pādau viharaṇam |
pāyurvisargam |
upasthamānandam |
ubhayātmakaṃ manaḥ |
svasaṃkalpavikalpavṛttī kurute |
evanekādaśendriyāṇi vyākhyātāni |
athaiṣāṃ paryāyāḥ |
indriyāṇi karaṇāni vaikārikāṇi khāni niyatāni padāni avadhṛtāni aṇūni akṣāṇīti |
body.translated_text: Now, what are those sixteen modifications (<s>vikāras</s>)? To this it is said: The eleven sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>) and the five great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) — these are the sixteen modifications. Among these, the sense-organs are first explained: Hearing (<s>śrotra</s>), skin (<s>tvak</s>), sight (<s>cakṣus</s>), tongue (<s>jihvā</s>), and smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) — these are the five organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyas</s>). Hearing grasps its own object, sound; skin [grasps] the object of touch; sight [grasps] the object of form; the tongue [grasps] the object of taste; smell [grasps] the object of odor. The five organs of action (<s>karmendriyas</s>), called speech (<s>vāk</s>), hands (<s>pāṇi</s>), feet (<s>pāda</s>), anus (<s>pāyu</s>), and generative organ (<s>upastha</s>), each perform their respective actions. Among these, speech utters words; the hands perform work; the feet [perform] locomotion; the anus [performs] excretion; the generative organ [provides] pleasure. The mind (<s>manas</s>), which partakes of the nature of both [knowledge and action organs], performs its own function of intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) and deliberation (<s>vikalpa</s>). Thus the eleven sense-organs have been explained. Now, their synonyms: <s>indriyas</s> (sense-organs), <s>karaṇas</s> (instruments), <s>vaikārikas</s> (modifications), <s>khas</s> (apertures), <s>niyatas</s> (regulated), <s>padas</s> (stations), <s>avadhṛtas</s> (determined), <s>aṇus</s> (subtle), and <s>akṣas</s> (axes). ||

body.text:
atha kāni pañcamahābhūtānītyatrocyate |
pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśānīti mahābhūtāni |
tatra pṛthivī dhāraṇabhāvena pravartamānā caturṇāmupakāraṃ karoti |
āpo jalāni saṃgrahabhāvena pravarttamānāścaturṇāmupakāraṃ kurvanti |
tejaḥ pācakabhāvena pravartamānaṃ caturṇāmupakāraṃ karoti |
vāyurvāhanabhāvena pravartamānaścaturṇāmupakāraṃ karoti |
ākāśamavakāśadānena pravartamānaṃ caturṇāmupakāraṃ karoti |
śabdasparśarūparasagandhavatī pañcaguṇā pṛthivī |
śabdasparśarūparasavatyaścaturguṇā āpaḥ |
śabdasparśarūpavat triguṇaṃ tejaḥ |
śabdasparśavān dviguṇo vāyuḥ |
śabdavadekaguṇamākāśam |
evamākhyātāni pañca mahābhūtāni |
athaiṣāṃ paryāyāḥ |
bhūtāni bhūtaviśeṣāḥ vikārāḥ ākṛtayaḥ tanavaḥ vigrahāḥ śāntāḥ ghorāḥ mūḍhāḥ ityete ṣoḍaśavikārā vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, what are the five great elements (<s>pañcamahābhūta</s>)? To this it is said: Earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>ap</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), wind (<s>vāyu</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>) — these are the great elements. Among them, earth, functioning through the mode of support (<s>dhāraṇa</s>), renders service to the [other] four. Water, functioning through the mode of cohesion (<s>saṃgraha</s>), renders service to the [other] four. Fire, functioning through the mode of cooking (<s>pācaka</s>), renders service to the [other] four. Wind, functioning through the mode of carrying (<s>vāhana</s>), renders service to the [other] four. Space, functioning through the mode of providing room (<s>avakāśadāna</s>), renders service to the [other] four. Earth has five qualities: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. Water has four qualities: sound, touch, form, and taste. Fire has three qualities: sound, touch, and form. Wind has two qualities: sound and touch. Space has one quality: sound. Thus the five great elements have been described. Now their synonyms: elements (<s>bhūta</s>), specific elements (<s>bhūtaviśeṣa</s>), modifications (<s>vikāra</s>), forms (<s>ākṛti</s>), subtle [elements] (<s>tanu</s>), bodies (<s>vigraha</s>), calm (<s>śānta</s>), fierce (<s>ghora</s>), and deluding (<s>mūḍha</s>) — thus the sixteen modifications have been explained.

children.translated_text: [<s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 3 ||]

body.text:
athāha kaḥ puruṣa ityucyate |
puruṣo 'nādiḥ sūkṣmaḥ sarvagataścetano 'guṇo nityo draṣṭā bhoktā 'karttā kṣetravidamalo 'prasavadharmī ceti |
athāha kasmāt puruṣaḥ purāṇāt puriśayanāt purohitavṛttitvācca puruṣaḥ |
atha kasmādanādiḥ |
nāsyādiranto madhyo vā vidyata ityanādiḥ |
kasmāt sūkṣmaḥ |
niravayavatvādatīndriyatvāt sūkṣmaḥ |
kasmāt sarvagataḥ |
sarvaṃ prāptamanena nāsya gaganamastīti sarvagataḥ |
kasmāccetanaḥ |
sukhaduḥkamohopalabdhimattvāt |
kasmādaguṇaḥ |
sattvarajastamāṃsyasminna santyato 'guṇaḥ |
kasmānnityaḥ akṛtakatvādanutpādakatvācca |
kasmād draṣṭā |
prakṛtivikārānupalambhena iti |
kasmādbhoktā |
cetanabhāvāt sukhaduḥkhaparijñānācca |
kasmādakartā |
udāsīnatvādaguṇatvācca |
kasmāt kṣetravid |
kṣetrebhyo guṇān vettīti kṣetravid |
atha kasmādamalaḥ |
śubhāśubhakarmāṇyasmin puruṣe na santītyamalaḥ |
kasmādaprasavadharmī |
nirbījatvāt |
na kiñcidutpādayatītyarthaḥ |
evameṣa sāṃkhyapuruṣo vyākhyātaḥ |

children.translated_text: Now the synonyms of this <s>Puruṣa</s>:

children.text: puruṣaḥ ātmā pumān puṃguṇaḥ bahulaḥ jantuḥ jīvaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ naraḥ kaviḥ brahma akṣaraḥ prāṇaḥ ajaḥ yaḥ kaḥ saḥ eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Ātman</s> (self), <s>Pumān</s> (male), <s>Puṃguṇa</s> (male quality), <s>Bahula</s> (manifold), <s>Jantu</s> (being), <s>Jīva</s> (life), <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), <s>Nara</s> (man), <s>Kavi</s> (seer), <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Akṣara</s> (imperishable), <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), <s>Aja</s> (unborn), and the pronouns <s>yaḥ</s>, <s>kaḥ</s>, <s>saḥ</s>, <s>eṣaḥ</s>.
Thus these twenty-five principles (<s>tattva</s>) have been explained:
Eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (primal natures), sixteen modifications (<s>vikāra</s>), and <s>Puruṣa</s>.

body.translated_text: Now he asks: What is <s>Puruṣa</s>? It is said: <s>Puruṣa</s> is beginningless (<s>anādi</s>), subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), all-pervading (<s>sarvagata</s>), conscious (<s>cetana</s>), without qualities (<s>aguṇa</s>), eternal (<s>nitya</s>), the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>), the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), the non-doer (<s>akartṛ</s>), the knower of the field (<s>kṣetravid</s>), stainless (<s>amala</s>), and of non-productive nature (<s>aprasavadharmin</s>). Now why is he called <s>Puruṣa</s>? Because he is ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>), because he dwells in the city [of the body] (<s>puriśayana</s>), and because he functions like a priest (<s>purohitavṛttitva</s>) — therefore <s>Puruṣa</s>. Why beginningless? Because no beginning, end, or middle of him can be found — therefore beginningless. Why subtle? Because of being partless (<s>niravayavatva</s>) and beyond the senses (<s>atīndriyatva</s>) — therefore subtle. Why all-pervading? Because everything is pervaded by him, there is no space that is his [exclusive domain] — therefore all-pervading. Why conscious? Because of possessing the apprehension of pleasure, pain, and delusion. Why without qualities? Because <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> do not exist in him — therefore without qualities. Why eternal? Because of being unmade (<s>akṛtaka</s>) and non-productive (<s>anutpādaka</s>). Why the seer? Because of the perception of the modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). Why the experiencer? Because of being conscious and because of the complete knowledge of pleasure and pain. Why the non-doer? Because of being indifferent (<s>udāsīna</s>) and without qualities. Why the knower of the field? Because from the fields [i.e., bodies], he knows the qualities — therefore the knower of the field. Why stainless? Because good and bad actions do not exist in this <s>Puruṣa</s> — therefore stainless. Why of non-productive nature? Because of being seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) — the meaning is that he does not produce anything. Thus this <s>Sāṃkhya Puruṣa</s> has been explained.

children.translated_text: One who knows the twenty-five principles, whether delighting in any <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) whatsoever,

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: whether wearing matted hair, shaven-headed, or with a topknot — he is liberated; of this there is no doubt.

body.text:
atrāha puruṣaḥ kiṃ kartā akarttā veti |
yadi karttā puruṣaḥ syāt tadā śubhāni kuryāt |

children.text: nanu vṛttitrayaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ puruṣasya tataḥ kiṃ guṇānāṃ kartṛtā 'siddhā ?
children.translated_text: But the three modes of conduct (<s>vṛttitraya</s>) are observed in the world for the person — hence how is the non-agency of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) not established?
That called <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), contentment, the observance of <s>yama</s> (restraint) and <s>niyama</s> (discipline), lucidity,
knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>), and dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), illumination — this is the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) mode of conduct.

body.translated_text: Here it is asked: Is this <s>Puruṣa</s> a doer (<s>kartṛ</s>) or a non-doer (<s>akartṛ</s>)? If <s>Puruṣa</s> were a doer, then he would perform good deeds.

children.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), fault-finding of others, excessive cruelty, discontentment,
distorted form and harshness — this is the well-known <s>rājasa</s> (passionate) mode of conduct.
Negligence (<s>pramāda</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), dejection (<s>viṣāda</s>), nihilism (<s>nāstikya</s>), addiction to women, sleep (<s>nidrā</s>),
laziness (<s>ālasya</s>), ruthlessness (<s>nairghṛṇya</s>), and impurity (<s>aśauca</s>) — this is the <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) mode of conduct.

body.text: etadvṛttitrayaṃ dṛṣṭvā loke guṇānāṃ kartṛtvaṃ siddhamiti cākarttā puruṣaḥ siddho bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Having observed these three modes of conduct in the world, the agency of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) is established, and thus <s>Puruṣa</s> is established as a non-doer.

children.translated_text: These <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), set in motion by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), through the distorted perception [caused] by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> —
the ignorant one thinks 'I am the doer,' [he who is] powerless even to bend a blade of grass.

children.text: sarvamidaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ mamedamiti vadannabhimānādabudha unmattaḥ kartṛvadbhavati atrāha |
children.translated_text: 'All this has been done by me, this is mine' — speaking thus from false identification (<s>abhimāna</s>), the ignorant, deluded person becomes as if a doer. Here it is said:
Actions are performed in all ways by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature);
the self, deluded by egoism (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), thinks 'I am the doer.'
Because of being beginningless, because of being without qualities, this supreme self (<s>Paramātman</s>) is imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>);

children.text: śarīrastho 'pi kauntaya na karoti na lipyate //
children.translated_text: though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, he neither acts nor is tainted.
Thus:
Actions are performed in all ways by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) alone;
he who sees the self thus as a non-doer — he truly sees.

body.text: tatrāha kimayamekaḥ puruṣo bahavo vetyucyate /
body.translated_text: Here it is asked: Is this <s>Puruṣa</s> one or many? It is said:

body.text:
sukhaduḥkhamohasaṅkaraviśuddhakaraṇapāṭavajanmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ nānātvāt puruṣabahutvaṃ siddhaṃ lokāśramavarṇabhedācca |
yadyekaḥ puruṣaḥ syādekasmin sukhini sarva eva sukhinaḥ syuḥ |
ekasmin duḥkhini sarva eva duḥkhinaḥ syuḥ |
ekasmin karaṇapāṭave sarveṣāmeva karaṇapāṭavaṃ syāt |
ekasmiñjāte sarva eva jāyeran |
ekasmin mṛte sarva eva mriyeranniti |
na caivam itaśca bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ siddhāḥ |
ākṛtigarbhāśayabhāvasaṅgatiśarīravibhāge liṅgabahutvāt |
evaṃ tāvat sāṃkhyācāryāḥ kapilāsuripañcaśikhapatañjaliprabhṛtayo bahūn puruṣān varṇayanti |

children.translated_text: The teachers who hold the <s>Vedānta</s> view — <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and others — describe the <s>Ātman</s> (self) as one alone.
Why is this so? To that he says:

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yacca bhāvyam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — whatever has been and whatever will be.
And he is the lord of immortality, who grows beyond through food.

body.translated_text: Due to the diversity of pleasure, pain, delusion, their admixture, purity, acuity of sense-organs, birth, and death — the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established; and also because of the distinctions of world (<s>loka</s>), stage of life (<s>āśrama</s>), and social class (<s>varṇa</s>). If <s>Puruṣa</s> were one, then when one is happy, all would be happy; when one suffers, all would suffer; when one has acuity of sense-organs, all would have such acuity; when one is born, all would be born; when one dies, all would die. But this is not so; hence many <s>Puruṣas</s> are established. [Also] because of the multiplicity of marks (<s>liṅga</s>) in the division of bodily forms, wombs, dispositions, natures, associations, and bodies. Thus, for now, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers — <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>, and others — describe multiple <s>Puruṣas</s>.

children.translated_text: That indeed is <s>Agni</s> (fire), that is <s>Āditya</s> (sun), that is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), that indeed is the moon (<s>Candramās</s>).

children.text: tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadāpaḥ saḥ prajāpatiḥ //
children.translated_text: That indeed is the pure (<s>śukra</s>), that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is the waters, that is <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures).

body.text: tadeva satyamamṛtaṃ sa mokṣaḥ sā parā gatiḥ //
body.translated_text: That indeed is truth, the immortal; that is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), that is the supreme goal (<s>parā gati</s>).

body.text:
tadakṣaraṃ tat saviturvareṇyaṃ
  yasmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiñcit //
body.translated_text: That is the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), that is the most excellent of <s>Savitṛ</s> (the sun), beyond which there is nothing higher or other whatsoever.

children.text: yasmānnāṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kaścid vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhatyekastenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam |
children.translated_text: Than which there is nothing smaller nor anything greater — like a tree he stands firm in heaven, the One. By that <s>Puruṣa</s> all this is pervaded.
With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
with ears everywhere in the world — he stands enveloping all.
Reflecting the qualities of all senses, yet devoid of all senses,
the lord and ruler of all, the great refuge of all.
Of all [things] everywhere, of all principles, the self of all, the source of all,

children.text: sarvaṃ vilīyate yasmin tadbrahma munayo viduḥ //
children.translated_text: that in which everything dissolves — the sages know that as <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: eka eva hi bhūtātmā dehe dehe vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one self of beings (<s>bhūtātman</s>) alone is established in every body;
it appears as one and as many, like the moon [reflected] in water.

children.text: sa hi sarveṣu bhūteṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca /
children.translated_text: For in all beings, movable and immovable,
this one great self dwells, by which all this is pervaded.
This self of the world is one; by that one it has been made manifold.
They speak of the self as separate in the production of knowledge and the like.
In a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in worms and insects, in a <s>śvapāka</s> (outcaste), in a dog, in an elephant,
in cattle, cows, gadflies, and mosquitoes — the wise see [the self] as equal.

children.text: eka eva yathā sūtraṃ suvarṇe vartate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a single thread runs through gold, and again
through pearls, gems, coral, clay, and silver —
so too in cows and humans, likewise in elephants, deer, and other [creatures],
this one self should be known as established everywhere.
[The three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 4 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kiṃ traiguṇyaṃ nāmocyate |
sattvarajastamāṃsīti triguṇā eva traiguṇyam |
sattvaṃ nāma prasādalāghavaprasannatābhiṣaṅgaprītituṣṭititikṣāsantoṣādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsataḥ sukhātmakam |
rajo nāma śokatāpasvedastambhodvegaroṣamānādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsato duḥkhātmakam |

children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is characterized by covering (<s>ācchādana</s>), veiling (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), loathsomeness (<s>bībhatsa</s>), wretchedness (<s>dainya</s>), heaviness (<s>gaurava</s>), laziness (<s>ālasya</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), and the like — of infinite varieties, [but] in brief, its essence is delusion (<s>moha</s>).
This <s>traiguṇya</s> (triple quality) has been explained.
One should know <s>sattva</s> as that which illuminates, <s>rajas</s> as that which activates,
and <s>tamas</s> as that which obscures — this is called <s>traiguṇya</s> (the threefold quality).

body.translated_text: Here it is asked: What is called the 'triple quality' (<s>traiguṇya</s>)? It is said: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these three <s>guṇas</s> alone constitute <s>traiguṇya</s>. <s>Sattva</s> is characterized by clarity (<s>prasāda</s>), lightness (<s>lāghava</s>), serenity (<s>prasannatā</s>), attachment, delight (<s>prīti</s>), contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), forbearance (<s>titikṣā</s>), satisfaction (<s>santoṣa</s>), and the like — of infinite varieties, [but] in brief, its essence is pleasure (<s>sukha</s>). <s>Rajas</s> is characterized by grief (<s>śoka</s>), burning (<s>tāpa</s>), perspiration (<s>sveda</s>), rigidity (<s>stambha</s>), agitation (<s>udvega</s>), fury (<s>roṣa</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and the like — of infinite varieties, [but] in brief, its essence is pain (<s>duḥkha</s>).

children.translated_text: [Evolution (<s>sañcara</s>). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 5 ||]
[Involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 6 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kaḥ sañcaraḥ pratisañcaraśca |
atrocyate |
utpattiḥ sañcaraḥ pralayaḥ pratisañcaraḥ |
tatrotpattirnāmāvyaktāt prāgupadiṣṭāt sarvataḥ puruṣeṇa pareṇādhiṣṭhitā buddhirutpadyate |
aṣṭaguṇā buddhiḥ |
buddhitattvādahaṅkāra utpadyate |
sa cāhaṃkārastrividho vaikārikastaijaso bhūtādiriti |
tatra vaikārikādahaṃkārādeva indriyāṇi cotpadyante |
bhūtādestanmātrāṇi |
taijasādubhayam |
tanmātrebhyo bhūtānīti sañcaraḥ |
pratisañcaro nāma bhūtāni tanmātreṣu līyante |
tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāhaṃkāre |
ahaṃkāro buddhau |
buddhiravyakte |
tadavyaktaṃ kvacinna līyate |
kasmādanutpadyamānatvāt prakṛtiṃ puruṣañcaiva viddhyanādi ityevaṃ pratisañcaro vyākhyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is evolution (<s>sañcara</s>) and what is involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>)? To this it is said: Origination is evolution (<s>sañcara</s>); dissolution is involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>). Therein, origination means: from the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>) previously described, presided over in all respects by the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Buddhi</s> (Intellect) arises. <s>Buddhi</s> has eight forms. From the <s>Buddhi</s>-principle, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) arises. And that <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> is threefold: <s>Vaikārika</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Bhūtādi</s>. Therein, from the <s>Vaikārika</s> form of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, the sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>) arise. From <s>Bhūtādi</s>, the subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) [arise]. From <s>Taijasa</s>, both [arise]. From the <s>tanmātras</s>, the [gross] elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) [arise] — this is evolution (<s>sañcara</s>). Involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>) means: the [gross] elements dissolve into the <s>tanmātras</s>; the <s>tanmātras</s> and the sense-organs [dissolve] into <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>; <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> [dissolves] into <s>Buddhi</s>; <s>Buddhi</s> [dissolves] into the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>). That Unmanifest does not dissolve anywhere. Why? Because it is unproduced — 'Know that <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are both beginningless.' Thus involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>) has been explained.

children.translated_text: [The subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_7 ||]

body.text:
tatrāha kiṃ tadadhyātmamadhibhūtamadhidaivataṃ ceti |
tatrocyate |
buddhiradhyātmam boddhavyamadhibhūtaṃ brahmā tatrādhidaivatam |
ahaṃkāro 'dhyātmaṃ mantavyamadhibhūtaṃ rudrastatrādhidaivatam |
mano 'dhyātmaṃ saṃkalpitavyamadhibhūtaṃ candrastatrādhidaivatam |
śrotramadhyātmaṃ śrotavyamadhibhūtamākāśastatrādhidaivatam |
tvagadhyātmaṃ sparśayitavyamadhibhūtaṃ vāyustatrādhidaivatam |
cakṣuradhyātmaṃ draṣṭavyamadhibhūtamādityastatrādhidaivatam |
jihvādhyātmaṃ rasayitavyamadhibhūtaṃ varuṇastatrādhidaivatam |
ghrāṇamadhyātmaṃ ghrātavyamadhibhūtaṃ pṛthvī tatrādhidaivatam |
vāgadhyātmaṃ vaktavyamadhibhūtaṃ agnistatrādhidaivatam |
pāṇī adhyātmaṃ grahītavyamadhibhūtamindrastatrādhidaivatam |
pādāvādhyātmaṃ gantavyamadhibhūtaṃ viṣṇustatrādhidaivatam |
pāyuradhyātmamutsraṣṭavyamadhibhūtaṃ mitrastatrādhidaivatam |
upasthamadhyātmamānandayitavyamadhibhūtaṃ prajāpatistatrādhidaivatam |
evametat trayodaśavidhasya karaṇasyādhyātmamadhibhūtamadhidaivataṃ vyākhyātam |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is that — the subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>)? To this it is said: <s>Buddhi</s> is the subjective; what is to be known is the objective; <s>Brahmā</s> is the presiding deity there. <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> is the subjective; what is to be thought is the objective; <s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity there. <s>Manas</s> (mind) is the subjective; what is to be imagined is the objective; <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) is the presiding deity there. The ear (<s>śrotra</s>) is the subjective; what is to be heard is the objective; space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the presiding deity there. The skin (<s>tvak</s>) is the subjective; what is to be touched is the objective; wind (<s>vāyu</s>) is the presiding deity there. The eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is the subjective; what is to be seen is the objective; the sun (<s>āditya</s>) is the presiding deity there. The tongue (<s>jihvā</s>) is the subjective; what is to be tasted is the objective; <s>Varuṇa</s> is the presiding deity there. The nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) is the subjective; what is to be smelled is the objective; the earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>) is the presiding deity there. Speech (<s>vāk</s>) is the subjective; what is to be spoken is the objective; <s>Agni</s> (fire) is the presiding deity there. The hands (<s>pāṇi</s>) are the subjective; what is to be grasped is the objective; <s>Indra</s> is the presiding deity there. The feet (<s>pāda</s>) are the subjective; what is to be traversed is the objective; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the presiding deity there. The anus (<s>pāyu</s>) is the subjective; what is to be excreted is the objective; <s>Mitra</s> is the presiding deity there. The generative organ (<s>upastha</s>) is the subjective; what is to be enjoyed is the objective; <s>Prajāpati</s> is the presiding deity there. Thus, for this thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), the subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>) have been explained.

children.text: tattvāni yo vedayate yathāvad guṇasvarūpāṇyadhidaivataṃ ca /
children.translated_text: He who truly knows the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) as they are — with their qualities, essential natures, and presiding deities —

children.text: vimuktapāpmā gatadoṣasaṅgho guṇāṃstu bhuṅkte na guṇaiḥ sa bhajyate //
children.translated_text: freed from sin, with the stain of faults removed, he enjoys the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) but is not broken by the <s>guṇas</s>. //
[The five modes of awareness (<s>abhibuddhis</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_8 ||]

body.text:
atha kāstāḥ pañcābhibuddhaya ucyate |
vyavasāyo 'bhimānecchā kartavyatā kriyeti |
abhimukhī buddhiridaṃ karaṇīyaṃ mayeti vyavasāyo buddhikriyā |
ātmaparātmasvarūpapratyayābhimukho 'bhimāno 'haṃkāro buddheḥ kriyā |
icchā vāñchā saṅkalpo manaso buddhikriyā |
śabdādiviṣayālocanaśravaṇādilakṣaṇakartavyatā buddhīndriyāṇāṃ buddhikriyā |
vacanādilakṣaṇabuddhikriyā karmendriyāṇāṃ sā kriyeti |
evametāḥ pañcābhibuddhayo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, what are those five modes of awareness (<s>abhibuddhi</s>)? To this it is said: Determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>), self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), purposive activity (<s>kartavyatā</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>). The directed awareness (<s>abhimukhī buddhi</s>) that 'This is to be done by me' — this determination is the cognitive activity of <s>Buddhi</s>. The self-conceit directed toward the cognition of the nature of one's own self and others' selves — this <s>abhimāna</s> is the <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>'s cognitive activity of <s>Buddhi</s>. Desire (<s>icchā</s>), longing (<s>vāñchā</s>), and intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) are the cognitive activities of <s>Manas</s> (mind) belonging to <s>Buddhi</s>. The purposive activity characterized by apprehending, hearing, etc. with respect to objects such as sound etc. is the cognitive activity of <s>Buddhi</s> belonging to the organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyas</s>). The cognitive activity of <s>Buddhi</s> characterized by speaking etc. belonging to the organs of action (<s>karmendriyas</s>) — that is action (<s>kriyā</s>). Thus these five modes of awareness (<s>abhibuddhis</s>) have been explained.

children.translated_text: [The five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_9 ||]

body.text:
atha kāstāḥ pañcakarmayonaya ucyante |
dhṛtiḥ śraddhā sukhā 'vividiṣā vividiṣā ca pañcakarmayonayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, what are those five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>)? To this it is said: Steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), happiness (<s>sukhā</s>), non-desire to know (<s>avividiṣā</s>), and desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — [these are] the five sources of action.

children.translated_text: He who, having resolved upon external actions, protects what has been obtained,
being devoted to that and established in that — this is the mark of steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>). //

children.text: svādhyāyo brahmacaryaṃ ca yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: Study of the <s>Veda</s> (<s>svādhyāya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), performing sacrifice (<s>yajana</s>), officiating at sacrifice (<s>yājana</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>),

children.text: dānaṃ pratigraho homaḥ śraddhāyā lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: gift-giving (<s>dāna</s>), receiving gifts (<s>pratigraha</s>), and oblation (<s>homa</s>) — this is declared to be the mark of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). //
He who, for the sake of happiness, engages in the activities of <s>Brahman</s>, ritual action, and austerity,
ever devoted to expiatory rites — this [disposition] is declared to be happiness (<s>sukhā</s>). //

body.text: viṣayamadhumiśritāntaḥkāraṇatvamavividiṣā /
body.translated_text: Non-desire to know (<s>avividiṣā</s>) is the state of the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) being mixed with the honey of sense-objects.

children.translated_text: And the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) is the source of wisdom (<s>prajñāna</s>) for those established in meditation (<s>dhyānins</s>).

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca nityaṃ caivamacetanam /
children.translated_text: Oneness and separateness, eternality, unconsciousness,

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ satkāryamakṣobhyaṃ jñeyā vividiṣā ca sā //
children.translated_text: subtlety, the doctrine of pre-existent effect (<s>satkārya</s>), imperturbability — this should be known as that desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>). //

body.text: kāryakāraṇakṣayakarī vividiṣā prākṛtikī vṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: The desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) that destroys the [cycle of] cause and effect is a natural (<s>prākṛtikī</s>) disposition.

body.text:
dhṛtiḥ śraddhā sukhā 'vividiṣā catasro bandhāya vidiṣaikā mokṣāya |
evametā pañca karmayonayo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), happiness (<s>sukhā</s>), and non-desire to know (<s>avividiṣā</s>) — these four lead to bondage; the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) alone leads to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Thus these five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>) have been explained.

children.translated_text: [The five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_10 ||]

body.text: atrāha ke pañcavāyava ucyante |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what are the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>)? To this it is said:

body.text: prāṇopānaḥ samānaśca udāno vyāna eva ca |
body.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> —

body.text: ityete vāyavaḥ pañca śarīreṣu śarīriṇām |
body.translated_text: these are the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>) in the bodies of embodied beings.

body.text:
tatra prāṇo nāma vāyurmukhanāsikādhiṣṭhātā praṇayanātprakramaṇācca prāṇa ityabhidhīyate |
apāno nāma vāyurnābhyadhiṣṭhitāpanayanādadhogamanāccāpāna ityabhidhīyate |
samāno nāma vāyurhṛdadhiṣṭhātā samanayanāt saṅgamanācca samāna ityabhidhīyate |
udāno nāma vāyuḥ kaṇṭhādhiṣṭhātā ūrdhvagamanādutkramaṇāccodāna ityabhidhīyate |
vyāno nāma vāyuḥ sandhyadhiṣṭhātā vikṣepaṇādvijṛmbhaṇācca vyāna ityabhidhīyate |
iti pañcavāyavo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the vital breath that presides over the mouth and nostrils; it is called <s>Prāṇa</s> because of leading forth (<s>praṇayana</s>) and proceeding (<s>prakramaṇa</s>). <s>Apāna</s> is the vital breath that presides over the navel; it is called <s>Apāna</s> because of carrying away (<s>apanayana</s>) and downward movement (<s>adhogamana</s>). <s>Samāna</s> is the vital breath that presides over the heart; it is called <s>Samāna</s> because of bringing together (<s>samanayana</s>) and uniting (<s>saṅgamana</s>). <s>Udāna</s> is the vital breath that presides over the throat; it is called <s>Udāna</s> because of upward movement (<s>ūrdhvagamana</s>) and departing upward (<s>utkramaṇa</s>). <s>Vyāna</s> is the vital breath that presides over the joints; it is called <s>Vyāna</s> because of dispersal (<s>vikṣepaṇa</s>) and stretching (<s>vijṛmbhaṇa</s>). Thus the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>) have been explained.

children.translated_text: [The five action-selves (<s>karmātmans</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_11 ||]

body.text:
atrāha ke te pañcakarmātmāna ityucyate |
vaikārikastaijaso bhūtādiḥ sānumāno niranumānaśca |
tatra vaikārikaḥ śubhakarmakartā |
taijaso 'śubhakarmakartā |
bhūtādirmūḍhakarmakartā |
sānumānaḥ śubhamūḍhakarmakartā |
niranumāno 'śubhamūḍhakarmakartā caivaṃ pañcakarmātmāno vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what are those five action-selves (<s>karmātmans</s>)? To this it is said: <s>Vaikārika</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, <s>Bhūtādi</s>, with inference (<s>sānumāna</s>), and without inference (<s>niranumāna</s>). Among these, the <s>Vaikārika</s> is the doer of virtuous actions. The <s>Taijasa</s> is the doer of unvirtuous actions. The <s>Bhūtādi</s> is the doer of deluded actions. The one with inference (<s>sānumāna</s>) is the doer of virtuous-deluded actions. The one without inference (<s>niranumāna</s>) is the doer of unvirtuous-deluded actions. Thus the five action-selves (<s>karmātmans</s>) have been explained.

children.translated_text: [Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) of five divisions. || <s>Tats</s>_12 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kā sā pañcaparvāvidyetyucyate |
tamo moho mahāmohastāmiśro 'ndhatamisraśceti |
tatra tamomohāvubhāvaṣṭātmakau |
mahāmoho daśātmakaḥ |
tāmisrondhatāmisraścāṣṭādaśātmakau |
tamo nāmāṣṭasu prakṛtiṣvavyaktabuddhyahaṃkārapañcatanmātrasaṃjñitāsvanātmasvātmābhimānastama ityabhidhīyate |
moho nāmāṇimādyaṣṭaiśvaryaprāptaye yo 'bhimāna utpadyate sa moha ityabhidhīyate |
mahāmoho nāma dṛṣṭānuśravikeṣu śabdādiviṣayeṣu daśasu vṛttiṣu muktohamiti manyate sa mahāmoha ityabhidhīyate |
tāmisro nāmāṣṭaguṇaiśvarye 'ṇimādye daśavidhe ca viṣaye yo dveṣo 'pratihatastatra yad duḥkhamutpadyate 'sau tāmisra ityabhidhīyate |
andhatāmisro nāmāṣṭaguṇaiśvarye 'ṇimādye daśavidhe ca viṣaye siddhe maraṇakāle yo viṣāda utpadyate so 'ndhatāmisra ityabhidhīyate |
evameṣā pañcaparvā 'vidyā dviṣaṣṭibhedā vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is that five-branched ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)? To this it is said: <s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>Moha</s> (delusion), <s>Mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>Andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness). Among these, <s>Tamas</s> and <s>Moha</s> each have eight forms. <s>Mahāmoha</s> has ten forms. <s>Tāmisra</s> and <s>Andhatāmisra</s> each have eighteen forms. <s>Tamas</s> means: the self-conceit (<s>ātmābhimāna</s>) that takes what is not the self to be the self with respect to the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> — namely, <s>Avyakta</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, and the five <s>tanmātras</s> — this is called <s>Tamas</s>. <s>Moha</s> means: the self-conceit that arises for the sake of attaining the eight supernatural powers (<s>aiśvaryas</s>) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) — this is called <s>Moha</s>. <s>Mahāmoha</s> means: with respect to the ten objects beginning with sound — both seen and heard of — in the ten modes of activity (<s>vṛttis</s>), [one who] thinks 'I am liberated' — this is called <s>Mahāmoha</s>. <s>Tāmisra</s> means: with respect to the eightfold sovereignty of powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, and the tenfold sense-objects, the aversion that is unimpeded, and the suffering that arises there — that is called <s>Tāmisra</s>. <s>Andhatāmisra</s> means: when the eightfold sovereignty of powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> and the tenfold sense-objects have been attained, the despair (<s>viṣāda</s>) that arises at the time of death — that is called <s>Andhatāmisra</s>. Thus this five-branched ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), with its sixty-two varieties, has been explained.

children.translated_text: [Incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) of twenty-eight kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_13 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kā sāṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiratrocyate |
ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ saptadaśa tuṣṭisiddhi(buddhi)vadhāḥ |
eṣāṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiriti |
tatrendriyavadhāstāvaducyante |
śrotre bādhiryaṃ jihvāyāṃ jaḍatvaṃ tvaci kuṣṭhitvaṃ cakṣuṣyarūpatvaṃ nāsikāyāmaghrāṇatvaṃ vāci mūkatvaṃ hastayoḥ kuṇitvaṃ pādayoḥ paṅgutvaṃ vāgindriya udāvarta upasthendriye klaibyaṃ manasyunmāda ityekādaśendriyavadhāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is that twenty-eight-fold incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>)? To this it is said: The eleven defects of the sense-organs (<s>indriya-vadhas</s>) and the seventeen defects of contentment and attainment (or cognition) (<s>tuṣṭi-siddhi/buddhi-vadhas</s>). This is the twenty-eight-fold incapacity. Among these, the defects of the sense-organs are first stated: Deafness in the ear; dullness in the tongue; leprosy in the skin; blindness in the eye; inability to smell in the nose; muteness in speech; deformity (<s>kuṇitva</s>) in the hands; lameness in the feet; incontinence (<s>udāvarta</s>) in the excretory organ; impotence (<s>klaibya</s>) in the generative organ; madness (<s>unmāda</s>) in the mind — these are the eleven defects of the sense-organs.

children.translated_text: [Contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) of nine kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_14 ||]
[Attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) of eight kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_15 ||]

body.text:
saptadaśatuṣṭisiddhivadhā nāma viparyayāstuṣṭisiddhīnām |
tuṣṭiviparyayāstāvaducyante |
tatra nāsti pradhānamiti yā pratipattiranantā |
evamahamityātmajñāne tāmasalīnā tathāhaṃkārasyādarśanamavidyā |
naiva santi tanmātrāṇi bhūtakāraṇānītyavṛṣṭiḥ |
viṣayāṇāmarjane pravṛttirasutārā |
rakṣaṇe tu pravṛttirasupārā ca |
kṣayadoṣamadṛṣṭvā 'rthe pravṛttirasunetrā |
bhogā śaktirasumarīcikā |
hiṃsādoṣamapaśyato bhogārambho 'nuttamāmbhasikā |
iti tuṣṭiviparyayā navadhā 'tuṣṭayo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: The seventeen defects of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) are the opposites (<s>viparyayas</s>) of contentment and attainment. The opposites of contentment are first stated: Therein, the conviction that 'the primal substance (<s>pradhāna</s>) does not exist' is called <s>Anantā</s> (endless [doubt]). Similarly, in the knowledge of the self as 'I am thus' — being absorbed in the dark quality (<s>tāmasa</s>) and the non-perception of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> — is <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance). [The view] that 'the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), which are the causes of the [gross] elements, do not exist at all' is <s>Avṛṣṭi</s> (barrenness). The inclination toward the acquisition of sense-objects is <s>Asutārā</s> (difficult to cross). The inclination toward their preservation is <s>Asupārā</s> (difficult to bridge). The inclination toward wealth without seeing the fault of its decay is <s>Asunetrā</s> (poorly guided). The capacity for enjoyment is <s>Asumarīcikā</s> (like a mirage). The commencement of enjoyment by one who does not see the fault of causing harm — this is <s>Anuttamāmbhasikā</s> (like [seeking in] a waterless [place]). Thus the opposites of contentment — the nine forms of discontentment (<s>atuṣṭi</s>) — have been explained.

body.text:
atha siddhiviparyayā asiddhayo 'ṣṭau cābhidhīyante |
nānātvaṃ bhūtamātrasyaikātvamāvirbhūtamatāramucyate |
śabdamātraśravaṇādviparītagrahaṇamāsutāraṃ yathā nānātvajño mukta iti śrutvā viparītaṃ pratipanno nānātvajño hyamukta iti |
adhyayanaśravaṇābhiniviṣṭasyāpi jaḍatvādasacchāstropahatabuddhitvādvā pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānasiddhirna bhavati tadā 'tāratāraṃ tadajñānam |
kasyacidādhyātmikena duḥkhenābhibhūtasyāpi saṃsāre 'nudvegādajijñāsorna jñānaṃ tatpramādam |
evamapramuditāpramodamānayoścānyonyayordvayamaparaṃ draṣṭavyam |
suhṛdupadiṣṭe 'pyaniścayabuddherajñānam parasparamasampā |
asampāvacanādathavā parāṅmukhe gurau durbhāgyasya jñānāsiddhistadajñānamasatpramuditamiti |
evamete siddhiviparyayā asiddhayo 'ṣṭau vyākhyātāḥ |
evameṣā 'ṣṭaviṃśatidhā 'śaktirvyākhyātā |
body.translated_text: Now, the reversals of attainment (<s>siddhiviparyaya</s>), the eight non-attainments (<s>asiddhis</s>), are described. The diversity of the elemental matrix — the oneness of [what has] become manifest is called <s>tāra</s> (the first [non-attainment]). From merely hearing a word, the erroneous apprehension is <s>sutāra</s> — for example, having heard 'one who knows diversity is liberated,' one erroneously concludes the opposite: 'one who knows diversity is indeed not liberated.' Even for one devoted to study and learning, due to dullness or due to having one's intellect corrupted by false scriptures, when the knowledge-attainment of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) does not occur, then that ignorance is <s>tāratāra</s>. For someone overcome by <s>ādhyātmika</s> (subjective) suffering, who, even while in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), has no sense of urgency and no desire to know — that knowledge [not arising] is <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness). Similarly, for [those in the states of] 'non-delighted' (<s>apramudita</s>) and 'non-rejoicing' (<s>apramodamāna</s>), the two [non-attainments] of each other should be seen as the remaining pair. For one of uncertain intellect, even when instructed by a friend, the ignorance is <s>mukhya</s> — <s>asampā</s> (non-communication). Or, by the word 'non-communication,' when the teacher is turned away [from the student], the non-attainment of knowledge for the unfortunate one — that ignorance is <s>asatpramudita</s> (false delight). Thus these eight non-attainments, reversals of attainment, have been explained. Thus this twenty-eight-fold incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) has been explained.

body.text:
atrāha kā sā navadhā tuṣṭiratrocyate |
prakṛtiṃ paramārthatvena parikalpya parituṣṭe mādhyasthaṃ labhate tasya tuṣṭyā sā tāntrikī saṃjñā 'mbha iti |
aparo buddhiṃ paramārthavena pratipadya parituṣṭastasyāstuṣṭeḥ śalilā iti saṃjñā |
anyo 'haṃkāraṃ paramārthatvenābhyupagamya parituṣṭastasyātuṣṭeḥ rodha iti saṃjñā |
itarastanmātrāṇi bhogyāni paramārthatvena viniścitya parituṣṭastasya tuṣṭervṛṣṭiriti saṃjñā |
evamādhyātmikyaścatasrastuṣṭayo bhavanti |
catasṛṣvapi tuṣṭiṣu nāsti mokṣastattvajñānasyāsambhavāt |
vāhyārthārjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādidoṣadarśanādviṣayoparame pañcatuṣṭayo bhavanti |
arthānāmarjane doṣadarśanāt tuṣṭaḥ pravrajitasyāpi nāsti mokṣastattvajñānābhāvāt |
sā pañcamī tuṣṭiḥ sutāretyabhidhīyate |
anyorthānāṃ rakṣaṇe doṣadarśanāt tuṣṭaḥ pravrajitasyāpi nāsti mokṣastattvajñānābhāvāt sā ṣaṣṭhī tuṣṭiḥ supāretyuṣyate |
anyorthānāṃ kṣayadoṣadarśanāt tuṣṭaḥ pravrajitasyāpi nāsti mokṣastattvajñānābhāvāt sā saptamī tuṣṭiḥ sunetretyabhidhīyate |
anyorthānāṃ saṅgadoṣadarśanāt tuṣṭaḥ pravrajitasyāpi nāsti mokṣastattvajñānābhāvāt sāṣṭamī tuṣṭiḥ sumarīciketyabhidhīyate |
anyo bhūtānāmarthanimittaṃ hiṃsādidoṣadarśanānnivṛttastuṣṭaḥ pravrajitasyāpi nāsti mokṣastattvajñānābhāvāt sā navamī tuṣṭiruttamāmbhasiketyabhidhīyate |
ityetā navatuṣṭayo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is that nine-fold contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>)? To this it is said: One who, having conceived <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) as the ultimate reality, is content — through that contentment he attains a state of indifference (<s>mādhyasthya</s>). The designation of that contentment is <s>tāntrikī</s>, called <s>ambha</s> (water). Another, having understood <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) as the ultimate reality, is content — the designation of that contentment is <s>śalilā</s> (fluid). Yet another, having accepted <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) as the ultimate reality, is content — the designation of that contentment is <s>rodha</s> (obstruction). Still another, having ascertained the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the objects of enjoyment, as the ultimate reality, is content — the designation of that contentment is <s>vṛṣṭi</s> (rain). Thus there are four internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) contentments. In all four contentments there is no liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), because the knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) does not arise. From seeing the faults such as violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) etc. in the acquisition, protection, loss, and attachment regarding external objects, upon turning away from sense objects, five contentments arise. One who is content from seeing faults in the acquisition of wealth — even for that renunciant there is no liberation, due to the absence of <s>tattva</s>-knowledge. That fifth contentment is called <s>sutāra</s>. Another who is content from seeing faults in the protection of wealth — even for that renunciant there is no liberation, due to the absence of <s>tattva</s>-knowledge. That sixth contentment is called <s>supāra</s>. Another who is content from seeing faults in the loss of wealth — even for that renunciant there is no liberation, due to the absence of <s>tattva</s>-knowledge. That seventh contentment is called <s>sunetra</s>. Another who is content from seeing faults in attachment to wealth — even for that renunciant there is no liberation, due to the absence of <s>tattva</s>-knowledge. That eighth contentment is called <s>sumarīcika</s>. Another who, having ceased from seeing faults such as violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) etc. caused by wealth toward beings, is content — even for that renunciant there is no liberation, due to the absence of <s>tattva</s>-knowledge. That ninth contentment is called <s>uttamāmbhasika</s>. Thus these nine contentments have been explained.

body.text:
atrāha kāṣṭau siddhaya ityatrocyate |
yadūhane jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā prathamā siddhistāreyabhidhīyate |
yacchabdamātreṇa jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā siddhiḥ sutāretyabhidhīyate |
yadadhyayanena jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā tṛtīyā siddhistārayantītyabhidhīyate |
yadādhyātmikasya duḥkhasyāpanodanaṃ kṛtvā jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā caturthī siddhiḥ pramuditetyabhidhīyate |
yadādhibhautikasya duḥkhasyāpanodanaṃ kṛtvā jñānam utpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā pañcamī siddhiḥ pramuditetyabhidhīyate |
yadādhidaivikasya duḥkhasyāpanodanaṃ kṛtvā jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā ṣaṣṭhī siddhiḥ pramodamānetyabhidhīyate |
yattu snigdhasaṃsargāvyapayājjñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu sā sapramī siddhiḥ ramyaketyabhidhīyate |
yat paricaryādānena jñānamutpadyate tattvabhāvabhūteṣu paritoṣite gurau siddhiḥ satpramuditetyabhidhīyate |
ityetā aṣṭasiddhayo vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what are the eight attainments (<s>siddhis</s>)? To this it is said: When knowledge arises through reasoning (<s>ūhana</s>) regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), that is the first attainment, called <s>tāra</s>. When knowledge arises through mere hearing of words regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that attainment is called <s>sutāra</s>. When knowledge arises through study (<s>adhyayana</s>) regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that is the third attainment, called <s>tārayantī</s>. When knowledge arises after removing <s>ādhyātmika</s> (subjective) suffering regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that is the fourth attainment, called <s>pramudita</s> (delighted). When knowledge arises after removing <s>ādhibhautika</s> (objective/elemental) suffering regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that is the fifth attainment, called <s>pramudita</s> (delighted). When knowledge arises after removing <s>ādhidaivika</s> (divine/supernatural) suffering regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that is the sixth attainment, called <s>pramodamāna</s> (rejoicing). When knowledge arises due to the association with affectionate [teachers] and non-separation [from them] regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, that is the seventh attainment, called <s>ramyaka</s> (delightful). When knowledge arises through the offering of service, when the teacher is gratified, regarding the true nature of the <s>tattvas</s>, the attainment is called <s>satpramudita</s> (truly delighted). Thus these eight attainments have been explained.

children.translated_text: [The fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>) of ten kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_16 ||]
Here one asks: what are the ten fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>)? To this it is said:
Existence (<s>astitva</s>), oneness (<s>ekatva</s>), purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>), other-directedness (<s>parārthatva</s>), difference (<s>anyatva</s>), and non-agency (<s>akartṛtā</s>),

children.text: yogo viyogo vahavaḥ pumāṃsaḥ sthitiḥ śarīrasya ca śeṣavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: union (<s>yoga</s>), separation (<s>viyoga</s>), multiplicity of <s>puruṣas</s>, and the residual activity of the body (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>) —

body.text: ityete daśamūlikārthāḥ |
body.translated_text: these are the ten fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthas</s>).

body.text:
saṅghātaparārthatvāditi puruṣāstitvaṃ siddham |
bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt kāraṇamastyavyaktamiti paryāyadvayena pradhānasyāstitvaṃ siddham |
hetumadanityamityekatvaṃ siddham |
prītyaprītiviṣādātmakā ityarthavattvaṃ siddham |
nānāvidhairupāyairiti parārthatvaṃ siddham |
triguṇamaviveki viṣaya ityanyatvaṃ siddham |
tasmācca viparyāsādityakartṛtvaṃ siddham |
puruṣasya darśanārthaṃ kaivalyārthaṃ tathā pradhānasyāpīti yogasiddhiḥ |
prāpte śarīrabhede caritārthatvāditi viyogasiddhiḥ |
janmamaraṇakaraṇānāmiti puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham |
cakrabhramivaditi śeṣavṛttiḥ siddhā |
ete daśamūlikārthā vyākhyātāḥ |
eteṣāṃ daśānāṃ prāgupadiṣṭānāṃ ca pañcāśatpratyayāḥ |
ete ca ṣaṣṭipadārthāḥ ṣaṣṭitantramityucyate |
body.translated_text: From [the sūtra] 'because the aggregate is for the sake of another' — the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self) is established. From [the sūtra] 'the cause exists because of the finitude of modifications' — through two alternative expressions, the existence of <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal substance) is established. From [the sūtra] 'because it is caused and non-eternal' — oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion' — purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'by various means' — other-directedness (<s>parārthatva</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'the three <s>guṇas</s> are non-discriminating and objective' — difference (<s>anyatva</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'and from that, the reverse' — non-agency (<s>akartṛtva</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s seeing, and for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), likewise of <s>Pradhāna</s>' — the attainment of union (<s>yoga</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'when bodily separation has occurred, because the purpose has been fulfilled' — the attainment of separation (<s>viyoga</s>) is established. From [the sūtra] 'because of [the diversity of] birth, death, and instruments' — the multiplicity of <s>puruṣas</s> is established. From [the sūtra] 'like the whirling of a wheel' — residual activity (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>) is established. These ten fundamental topics have been explained. These ten, together with the previously described fifty categories (<s>pratyayas</s>), [make up] sixty topics (<s>ṣaṣṭipadārthas</s>). And these are the sixty topics — [hence the system] is called <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (the Doctrine of Sixty [Topics]).

children.translated_text: [The creation for the sake of [divine] favor (<s>anugrahasarga</s>). || <s>Tats</s>_17 ||]

body.text:
atrāha ko 'nugrahasargaḥ atrocyate |
bāhyān pañcatanmātrebhyaścotpādyānugrahasargadhyānotpannenādhāravarjitān putrān dṛṣṭvā tebhyastanmātrebhyo 'nugrahasargamasṛjadbrahmā |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is the <s>anugrahasarga</s> (creation for [divine] favor)? To this it is said: <s>Brahmā</s>, having produced from the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) the external [creations] through meditation-born <s>anugrahasarga</s>, and having seen the offspring who were without support, created from those <s>tanmātras</s> the creation for [their] favor (<s>anugrahasarga</s>).

children.translated_text: [The creation of beings (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) of fourteen kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_18 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kaścaturdaśavidho bhūtasarga ityatrocyate |
aṣṭavikalpo daivaḥ paiśāco rākṣaso yākṣo gāndharva aindraḥ prājāpatyo brāhma ityaṣṭau devayonayaḥ |
pañcadhā tiryagyonaśca paśupakṣimṛgasarīsṛpasthāvarā iti |
gavādimūṣakāntāḥ paśavaḥ |
garuḍādimaśakāntāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ |
siṃhādiśṛgālāntāḥ mṛgāḥ |
śeṣādikīṭāntāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ |

children.translated_text: The immovable beings (<s>sthāvara</s>) range from mountains etc. to grass.
And the human (<s>mānuṣya</s>) creation is of one kind, ranging from <s>brāhmaṇas</s> etc. to <s>cāṇḍālas</s>.
The divine creation is of eight varieties, and the animal creation (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) is five-fold.
And the human creation is of one kind — in summary, this is the elemental creation (<s>bhautika sarga</s>). ||

body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is the fourteen-fold creation of beings (<s>bhūtasarga</s>)? To this it is said: The divine creation is of eight varieties: <s>daiva</s> (celestial), <s>paiśāca</s> (of <s>piśācas</s>), <s>rākṣasa</s> (of <s>rākṣasas</s>), <s>yākṣa</s> (of <s>yakṣas</s>), <s>gāndharva</s> (of <s>gandharvas</s>), <s>aindra</s> (of <s>Indra</s>'s realm), <s>prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>'s realm), and <s>brāhma</s> (of <s>Brahmā</s>'s realm) — these are the eight divine births. The animal creation (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) is five-fold: domestic animals (<s>paśu</s>), birds (<s>pakṣi</s>), wild animals (<s>mṛga</s>), reptiles (<s>sarīsṛpa</s>), and immovable beings (<s>sthāvara</s>). The domestic animals range from cows etc. to mice. The birds range from <s>Garuḍa</s> etc. to mosquitoes. The wild animals range from lions etc. to jackals. The reptiles range from <s>Śeṣa</s> etc. to insects.

children.translated_text: [The elemental creation (<s>dhātusarga</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_19 ||]

body.text:
samāsato ye tridhāḥ sargāḥ tatrāha kastrividho dhātusargaḥ atrocyate sūkṣmāḥ mātāpitṛjāḥ prabhūtā iti |
jñānendriyapañcaprāṇabuddhimanasāṃ gaṇaḥ sūkṣmaḥ |

children.translated_text: meaning the subtle bodies (<s>liṅgaśarīras</s>).

children.text: mātāpitṛjā ṣāṭkauśikāḥ tatra mātṛto lomalohitamāṃsāni pitṛtaḥ snāyvasthimajjāna iti ṣaṭko gaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: The born-of-parents [creation] consists of six sheaths (<s>ṣāṭkauśika</s>): from the mother come hair, blood, and flesh; from the father come sinew, bone, and marrow — this is the group of six.

children.text: prabhūtāḥ pañcamahābhūtāni mahābhūte ghaṭādīnāṃ niveśa iti trividho dhātusargo vyākhyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: The gross [creation] consists of the five great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) — within the great elements is the dwelling of pots and such [objects]. Thus the three-fold elemental creation (<s>dhātusarga</s>) has been explained.
Thus the circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) has been described. ||

body.translated_text: In summary, the creations are three-fold. Here one asks: what is the three-fold elemental creation (<s>dhātusarga</s>)? To this it is said: the subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), the born-of-parents (<s>mātāpitṛja</s>), and the gross (<s>prabhūta</s>). The group consisting of the five organs of knowledge (<s>jñānendriyas</s>), the five vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>), <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>Manas</s> (mind) is the subtle [creation] —

children.translated_text: [Bondage (<s>bandha</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_20 ||]

body.text:
atrāha kastrividho bandya ityatrocyate |
prakṛtibandho vaikārikabandho dakṣiṇābandhaśceti |
tatra prakṛtibandho nāmāṣṭau prakṛtayastāḥ paratenābhimanyamānasya prakṛtilayaḥ prakṛtibandha ityucyate |
tatra vaikārikabandho nāma pravrajitānāṃ laukikānāṃ vaikārikairindriyairvaśīkṛtānāṃ śabdādiviṣaye praśaktānāmajitendriyāṇāmajñānināṃ kāmamohitānāṃ vaikārikabandha ityucyate |
dakṣiṇābandho nāma brahmacārigṛhasthabhikṣuvaikhānasānāṃ kāmamohopahatacetasāmabhimānapūrvikāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ prayacchatāṃ dakṣiṇābandha ityucyate |
iti trividho bandho vyākhyātaḥ |
uktaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is the three-fold bondage (<s>bandha</s>)? To this it is said: <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>Prakṛti</s>), <s>vaikārikabandha</s> (bondage to modifications), and <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to ritual gifts). Among these, <s>prakṛtibandha</s> means: the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (root-principles) — for one who regards them as the supreme [reality], dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>) is called <s>prakṛtibandha</s>. Among these, <s>vaikārikabandha</s> means: for renunciants and laypeople who are conquered by the modified (<s>vaikārika</s>) sense-organs, who are attached to the objects of sound etc., whose senses are uncontrolled, who lack knowledge, and who are deluded by desire — this is called <s>vaikārikabandha</s>. <s>Dakṣiṇābandha</s> means: for <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate students), householders (<s>gṛhasthas</s>), mendicants (<s>bhikṣus</s>), and forest-dwellers (<s>vaikhānasas</s>) whose minds are afflicted by desire and delusion, who offer ritual gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) preceded by pride — this is called <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s>. Thus the three-fold bondage has been explained. And it is said:

children.text: prākṛtena tu bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: By the bondage of <s>Prakṛti</s>, and likewise by that of modifications (<s>vaikārika</s>),
and thirdly by [the bondage of] ritual gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) — this bondage is declared. //
[Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_21 ||]

body.text: atrāha kastrividho mokṣa ityatrocyate |
body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is the three-fold liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)? To this it is said:

body.text: jñānodrekādindriyarāgopaśamāt kṛtsnakṣayācceti |

children.translated_text: Through the excellence of knowledge and through the subsiding of the passion of the senses, there occurs the destruction of one's own <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit); and from the destruction of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation/liberation) [ensues].
And it is said:

children.text: ādyo hi mokṣo jñānena dvitīyo rāgasaṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: The first liberation is through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); the second through the destruction of passion (<s>rāgasaṃkṣaya</s>) /
The third [type of liberation], through complete destruction [of all afflictions], has been explained as the characteristic of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). //

body.translated_text: Through the excellence of knowledge (<s>jñānodreka</s>), through the subsiding of the passion of the senses (<s>indriyarāgopaśama</s>), and through the destruction of all [accumulated karma] (<s>kṛtsnakṣaya</s>).

children.translated_text: [The means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_22 ||]

body.text:
kiṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇamityatrocyate |
dṛṣṭamanumānamāptavacanaṃ ceti etat trividhaṃ pramāṇam |
dṛṣṭaṃ tāvadvyākhyāyate yāvadindriyāṇāṃ pañcendriyārthāḥ pratyakṣā eva dṛṣṭam |
anumānam pramāṇaṃ liṅgadarśane jāyamānaṃ jñānam |
yathā meghodayena vṛṣṭiḥ sādhyate bakapaṅktibhiḥ salilam dhūmenāgniḥ tadanumānam |
pratyakṣeṇānumānena vā yortho na sādhyate sa āptavacanāt sādhyate |

children.text: yathendro devānāṃ rājā uttarāḥ kuravaḥ sauvarṇo meruḥ svarge 'psarasa iti |
children.translated_text: For example: '<s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods,' 'the <s>Uttarakurus</s> [exist],' '<s>Meru</s> is made of gold,' 'in heaven there are <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs).'

children.text: ta indrādayaḥ pratyakṣānumānāsādhyāśca vasiṣṭādayo munayo vadanti santīndrādayaḥ āgamopyasti |
children.translated_text: These [entities] such as <s>Indra</s> etc., which are not established by perception or inference — sages such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> etc. declare that <s>Indra</s> etc. exist; thus scripture (<s>āgama</s>) also [serves as a pramāṇa].
One who is devoted to his own duty, free from passion (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>),
possessed of knowledge, endowed with good character — such a person is to be known as an <s>āpta</s> (authoritative person). //

body.translated_text: What are the three kinds of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)? To this it is said: Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and authoritative testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>) — these are the three kinds of <s>pramāṇa</s>. First, perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) is explained: insofar as the objects of the five sense-organs are directly perceptible (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — that is perception. Inference is the <s>pramāṇa</s> that is the knowledge arising from the observation of a sign (<s>liṅga</s>). Just as rain is inferred from the rising of clouds, water from a line of herons, and fire from smoke — that is inference. Whatever object is not established by perception or by inference, that is established by authoritative testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>).

body.text:
evametat trividhaṃ pramāṇamabhihitam |
atrāha tena trividhena pramāṇena kiṃ sādhyate atrocyate |
yathā loke mānena prasthādinā dhānyāni mīyante |
tulayā candanādīni dravyāṇi |
evamanena tattvabhāvabhūtāni pramīyante |
trividhena duḥkhenābhibhūto brāhmaṇaḥ kapilamaharṣiśaraṇamupāgataḥ atrāha |
body.translated_text: Thus these three kinds of <s>pramāṇa</s> have been stated. Here one asks: what is established by these three kinds of <s>pramāṇa</s>? To this it is said: Just as in the world, grains are measured by the measure of <s>prastha</s> etc., and substances such as sandalwood etc. are [measured] by a balance — so by these [pramāṇas], the true nature of the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) is ascertained. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> overcome by the threefold suffering approached the great sage <s>Kapila</s> as his refuge. Here one asks:

children.translated_text: [Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) of three kinds. || <s>Tats</s>_23 ||]

body.text:
kiṃ trividhaṃ duḥkhamityatrocyate |
ādhyātmikamādhibhautikamādhidaivikamiti |
tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvividhaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ceti |
śarīre bhavaṃ śārīram manasi bhavaṃ mānasaṃ ceti |
tatra śārīraṃ nāma vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ vaiṣamyādyadduḥkhamutpadyate jvarātisāravisūcikāmūrchādikaṃ tacchārīramucyate |
kāmakrodhalobhamohamaderṣyādikaṃ priyaviyogādikaṃ tanmānasamityucyate |
adhibhūtebhyo bhavamādhibhautikam |
mānuṣapaśumṛgasarīsṛpasthāvarebhyo yadduḥkhamutpadyate tadādhibhautikam |
adhidevebhyo jātamādhidaivikam |
śītoṣṇavātavarṣāsannipātādinimittaṃ yadduḥkhamutpadyate tadādhidaivikam |
anena trividhena duḥkhenābhibhūtasya brāhmaṇasya jijñāsotpanā |

children.translated_text: The desire to know is <s>jijñāsā</s> (the desire for knowledge).
Just as the desire of a thirsty person to drink water is thirst (<s>pipāsā</s>).
This, in brief, is the knowledge that leads to the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
Having known which, there would be no rebirth (<s>punarjanma</s>). ||

body.translated_text: What is the threefold suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>)? To this it is said: The subjective (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), the external-elemental (<s>ādhibhautika</s>), and the divine (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). Among these, the subjective (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) is of two kinds: bodily (<s>śārīra</s>) and mental (<s>mānasa</s>). That which arises in the body is bodily; that which arises in the mind is mental. Among these, bodily [suffering] is the suffering that arises from the imbalance of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) — fever, dysentery, cholera, fainting, etc. — that is called bodily. Desire (<s>kāma</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), etc., and the separation from the beloved etc. — that is called mental. That which arises from external beings (<s>adhibhūta</s>) is <s>ādhibhautika</s>. Whatever suffering arises from humans, domestic animals, wild animals, reptiles, and stationary beings — that is <s>ādhibhautika</s>. That which arises from divine sources (<s>adhideva</s>) is <s>ādhidaivika</s>. Whatever suffering arises from the causes of cold, heat, wind, rain, and humoral disorders — that is <s>ādhidaivika</s>. In the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> overcome by this threefold suffering, the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>) arose.

children.translated_text: This is the wisdom (<s>vijñāna</s>) of the great sage, the great-souled (<s>mahātman</s>) <s>Kapila</s>,
having heard which, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> attained the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>) and became one who had accomplished his purpose. //
This illumination of the sequence [of topics] (<s>kramadīpikā</s>) has been expounded following the order of the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> aphorisms.
And here, three hundred verses in the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> meter are to be known. //

body.text: iti śrītattvasamāsākhyā sūtravṛttiḥ samāptā ||
body.translated_text: Thus the commentary (<s>sūtravṛtti</s>) on the glorious <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> is completed. ||
